SOURCE: "GPTScore: Evaluate as You Desire", Jinlan Fu, See-Kiong Ng, Zhengbao Jiang, Pengfei Liu (NUS, CMU). The PDF is arXiv 2302.04166v2, dated 13 Feb 2023, and labelled "Preprint. Under review." Nothing in this PDF names a venue. I could not confirm NAACL 2024 from the source, so "(Fu et al., 2023, preprint)" in the note matches the version on file. If the course cites NAACL 2024, that needs a separate check against the published version, whose numbers may differ.

COVERAGE: I read all 98,539 chars, including Tables 1–16 and Appendices A–E. I only skimmed the references. About 13k chars are LaTeX blobs from the Figure 1 artwork, which I filtered out.

AUDIT OF THE NOTE (05-llm-as-judge.md, ~line 135)
- "19 models from 80M to 175B, 4 tasks, 22 aspects". Correct.
- "BARTScore's generation-probability idea". This is a fair description. The paper lists BARTScore (Yuan et al., 2021) in Table 7 as "BART Generation", and FED and HolisticEval also appear there as generation-probability metrics. The paper never says outright that it extends BARTScore. It reuses BARTScore's evaluation strategy and its "MT as paraphrasing" framing.
- "Naming the aspect ... 38.0 to 40.2". The numbers are correct and the metric is Spearman. Exact setup: Table 3, SummEval, COH aspect, sample-level Spearman. It is the Avg row over the 19 GPTScore variants, VAL (no instruction) vs IST (instruction, no demonstration). One wording problem: IST adds a task description plus an aspect definition, so it does more than name the aspect. "Only a little" is fair: the other Table 3 averages are CON 40.4→41.4, FLU 35.8→37.2, REL 31.3→32.2 and COV (RealSumm) 37.4→39.8. Note that the paper's own framing is that instruction "significantly improves the performance". Coherence is also not the largest gain.
- "text-davinci-003 usually correlated worse than davinci-001 (dialogue-level FED, 13.5 against 54.3)". The numbers are correct: Table 6, FED dialogue-level, Avg Spearman, d03 = 13.5 and d01 = 54.3. These are GPT3 variants only, with no instruction/demonstration split. "Usually" is the paper's own intro claim ("majority of the evaluation settings"). It is contradicted in summarization, where the paper says "GPT3-d03 performs better than GPT3-d01 significantly". The note should not suggest d03 loses everywhere.
- "Correlations stayed around 0.3–0.5". This is partly wrong. It holds for SummEval, RealSumm, MQM, BAGEL and SFRES (roughly 25–47, with MQM FLU only 10–16). It does not hold for NEWSROOM, where Table 13 shows GPTScore at about 60–74, or for QXSUM, which is about 9–28 and measured in Pearson per §5.1. On FED dialogue-level, d01 reaches 66.9 (DEP) and 62.8 (DIV). The note also mixes scales: tables report ×100 (38.0), while the note's range is 0–1.

LIMITS: Datasets were randomly subsampled "Due to the expensive API cost of GPT3", and the paper does not give the sample sizes. Dialogue was tested with GPT3 only. Evaluation is English-only, and MT is scored as paraphrase against the reference. The prompts were not explored ("leave a more comprehensive exploration on prompt engineering as a future work"). There is no limitations section. The method needs token log-probs, and the GPT3 completion models it relies on (a01–d03) are retired. Internal inconsistencies: 37 vs "9 datasets" (Appendix B), the swapped 40.8/5.5 values, and the INT values in Table 10 vs the prose.

BUILDS ON: BARTScore (Yuan et al., 2021); FED (Mehri & Eskénazi, 2020); PRISM (Thompson & Post, 2020); in-context learning (Brown et al., 2020; Min et al., 2022); FLAN instruction tuning (Chung et al., 2022); NaturalInstructions prompts (Wang et al., 2022); evaluation strategy from Yuan et al., 2021 and Zhang et al., 2022a.

CODE:
- Score definition (p3): "GPTScore(h|d,a,S) = Σ_{t=1}^{m} w_t log p(h_t|h<t, T(d,a,S), θ)". Here w_t is the token weight, and "we treat each token equally".
- Example prompt (Table 11, p17): "COH src->hypo Generate a coherent summary for the following text {src}\n\nTl;dr{hypo}"
- Dialogue prompts (Table 12) turn each aspect into a yes/no question that ends in "\nAnswer: Yes." and score the probability of "Yes".

FIGURES:
- Fig. 2 (p2), "The framework of GPTSCORE": shows how task specification, aspect definition and demonstrations combine into one template whose likelihood is scored. It is faster to read than the prose.
- Fig. 6 (p9), "Results of the GPT3 family models with different numbers of examples (K)": shows the demonstration plateau at a glance.
- Fig. 7 (p9): aspect-combination gains for INT.

PROBLEMS: The Figure 1 artwork extracts as long LaTeX base64 blobs, but nothing is lost. Some header labels are inconsistent: Table 13 lists NEWSROOM as COH/CON/FLU/REL, while Table 8 lists FLU/REL/INF/COH. Table 6 bolding did not come through. Page numbers come from per-page extraction. I found no embedded instructions.
